full_judgment: 4. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed learned Counsel for the appellant. has seriously assailed the High Court Division's interference with the lower Appellate Court's decision and contended that the question involved is whether the appellant is respondent's tenant in the suit premises and that this is purely a question of fact. This question he has contended was conclusively determined by the lower Appellate Court Division which being final judge of fact, interference with its decision by the High Court is palpably illegal and beyond its jurisdiction given under section 100 C.P.C. The interference has been criticized on the ground that the High Court Division reconsidered and re-assessed the, entire evidence in second appeal, as if it were a first appeal whereas such re-assessment and reconsideration of evidence on a question on fact is strictly prohibited by law. The learned Counsel has argued that there was no illegality in the decision of the lower Appellate Court nor was there any error or defect in the procedure followed by lower Appellate Court in arriving at its findings, and as such, reversal thereof in second appeal is unwarranted. In support of these contentions the learned Counsel has referred to a number of cases decided by superior Tribunals including, the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council, all of which are in agreement on the established principle that a finding of fact, however erroneous and inexcusable it might be, stands immune from interference in second appeal.
